title.rendered: What God Said, You Say — The Foundation | How to Declare Like Jesus Did, Day 1

excerpt.rendered: Jesus never guessed. He opened His mouth and said what the Father had already said — and heaven moved. Day 1 of a 14-day declaration devotional.

content.rendered:
Jesus never guessed. He never wished. He opened His mouth and said what the Father had already said — and heaven moved. The Gospel For Today begins a new fourteen-day journey into the sacred art of declaration, the Jesus-pattern of agreeing with heaven until earth rearranges itself.

The Gospel For Today | Sunday, October 18, 2026 | How to Declare Like Jesus Did, Day 1

Today’s Scripture

“You will also declare a thing, and it will be established for you; so light will shine on your ways.”
— Job 22:28 (NKJV)

“…God, who gives life to the dead and calls those things which do not exist as though they did.”
— Romans 4:17 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

Yesterday we closed the Teach Me How to Pray series and sat with Pray As You Go, the companion that taught us to turn our whole day into one unbroken conversation with God. Today we take a step deeper. Beyond asking, beyond even conversing, there is a holy art the Scriptures call declaration. In the NKJV, Job 22:28 says, “You will also declare a thing, and it will be established for you.” The Amplified Classic (AMPC) stretches it wider: “You shall decide and decree a thing, and it shall be established for you; and the light of God’s favour shall shine upon your ways.” And the Passion Translation (TPT) renders Romans 4:17 with equal power — Abraham’s God “calls into being things that don’t even exist yet.” That is the pattern Jesus walked in, and it is the pattern He now hands to us.

From Lagos to London, Manila to Nairobi, São Paulo to the quiet diaspora kitchens of the world, believers are rediscovering that prayer is not the only language of faith. There is a language that follows prayer — the language of agreement with what God has already said. In Lagos, a mother stands in her compound before dawn and declares peace over a child who has not yet come home. In London, a father on the Northern Line whispers that his household serves the Lord. In Manila, a nurse between wards decrees mercy over a patient. In Nairobi and São Paulo, young believers are learning that the mouth of a child of God is not a decoration — it is an instrument of the kingdom.

Jesus modelled this wherever He went. He did not ask the storm to be still — He told it to be still (Mark 4:39). He did not plead with Lazarus — He called him out (John 11:43). He did not debate the fig tree — He spoke to it (Mark 11:14). Almost every miracle in the Gospels begins with a sentence; and every one of those sentences begins with what the Father had already said. Jesus explained His own method plainly: “I have not spoken on My own authority; but the Father who sent Me gave Me a command, what I should say and what I should speak” (John 12:49, NKJV). That is the foundation of this series. We are not inventing fresh words. We are learning to say what God has already said.

Over the next fourteen mornings we will prophesy to dry bones, call light over our bodies and our minds, declare over our households and provision, speak over our work, silence the enemy, and set up standing declarations we can carry for the rest of our lives. Today we lay the foundation: what God said, you say. Pray As You Go closed with a short declaration for a reason — because prayer, prayed long enough, naturally rises into decree. From today, we learn how to let it rise on purpose.

The Pattern of Declaration

Acknowledge. Before you declare, you locate what God has already said in His Word. Declaration is not positive thinking; it is agreement with Scripture. “Faith comes by hearing, and hearing by the word of God” (Romans 10:17). Find the verse first — then stand on it.

Personalise. The Word was written for the whole Church, but faith makes it personal. “He loved me and gave Himself for me” (Galatians 2:20). You take the eternal whosoever of Scripture and write your name into it.

Proclaim. Then you open your mouth — not loud, but sure. Jesus often spoke softly to storms and dead bodies. The authority of declaration is not in volume; it is in the Word being spoken, and in the Name of Jesus being honoured.

Declaration

I declare and acknowledge that God has set the pattern, and I follow Him. Jesus never spoke on His own; He spoke what the Father said — and so do I. My mouth is an instrument of the kingdom, not of my fear. I decree a thing, and it is established for me; light shines on my ways. I call the things that are not as though they were, because I serve the God who gives life to the dead. I shut the mouth of every lying report, and I open my own mouth to agree with heaven. From this day forward I speak what God has spoken over me. I am not confused, I am not silent, and I am not afraid. In Jesus’ name. Amen.
